verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 5.1 E-6 ('No function loops without a bound'); 5.6 row 'Positions in an enumeration in the worker' (100000); decisions/RT-FIX-P3-residual-perf.md item (4); build-plan/red-team/RT-03-bounds-and-errors.md section 6 (a wait of more than a minute at a cap)
verdicts.evidence: pwd and toplevel: /home/user/mutation_game/.claude/worktrees/agent-ac1dd379a38113918 (branch worktree-agent-ac1dd379a38113918, HEAD aea1802). Ran git checkout --detach b9b8504c1b893dc73a25b46fe62382d59eb9cdf1; HEAD is b9b8504c1b893dc73a25b46fe62382d59eb9cdf1 and status was clean. Node v22.22.0. The lens branch worktree-agent-a5f6d9879d9bbf538 is at afdccab and only adds files (17 new files, no existing file changed). Applied packages/engine/test/unit/redteam-RT-03-hash.test.ts only. It imports only ../../src/index and no redteam/ file. It was absent at the gate commit. git status --porcelain: 'A  packages/engine/test/unit/redteam-RT-03-hash.test.ts'. npm --prefix <wt> ci --prefer-offline: exit 0. Ran the stated command from the worktree root three times: npx vitest run packages/engine/test/unit/redteam-RT-03-hash.test.ts --silent=false. Run 1, load 3.08 (the lowest seen in this session), exit 1: 'cap 40000: fast path from 2^30 rho 12890 ms; generic loop, same seed 522 ms; fast path from rho 93 ms' / 'AssertionError: expected 12889.870792 to be less than 2607.6814600000034' (24.7 times). Run 2, load 3.11 to 3.57, exit 1: '12720 ms; 569 ms; 88 ms' / 'expected 12719.532985000002 to be less than 2843.6031299999922' (22.4 times). Run 3, load 15.4 to 20.6, exit 1: '24482 ms; 1183 ms; 421 ms' (20.7 times). The item-equality assertion passed in every run, so the test failed only on the timing. Comparison: the finding says 20.3 to 20.7 s against 0.76 to 0.86 s at load 4 to 16, 24 to 27 times. I saw 12.7 to 24.5 s against 0.52 to 1.18 s, 20.7 to 24.7 times, with the same items. At the worker cap, in my script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-mutation-game/03d88ee7-3b55-5f84-9822-84f78aad9733/scratchpad/verify-rt03-reproduce/cap100k.cjs (engine compiled with tsc into scratch, load about 18 to 20): the 2^30 seed took 149.5 s on the fast path against 2.9 s on the generic loop, with the same 100000 items. The finding says 85.5 to 103.3 s against 2.7 s. Cause, by reading: search.ts:146-158 hashes each position as the sum over k of Math.imul(v[k]|0, R[k]) & 0x3fffffff. That is linear mod 2^30, so every multiple of 2^30 hashes to 0. The script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-mutation-game/03d88ee7-3b55-5f84-9822-84f78aad9733/scratchpad/verify-rt03-reproduce/collide.cjs hashes the engine's 40000 items with that formula. It also re-runs the fast path's firing loop with a counter of the chain walk; its items equal the engine's in every row. Results for E8 firing at cap 40000 from seed k(1,...,1), each with 164940 lookups: k=2^30 gives 1 distinct hash, bucket 40000, 1516547521 chain steps (9194.5 per lookup), fast 18642 ms, generic 855 ms. k=3*2^30 gives 1 hash and the same 1516547521 steps, fast 22519 ms. k=2^29 gives 2 hashes, largest bucket 20485, 758860210 steps, fast 11993 ms. k=2^30+1, with entries up to 1.29e10 (the same size as the 2^30 case), gives 2306 hashes, largest bucket 120, 1626545 steps (9.9 per lookup), fast 136 ms. k=1000003 and k=1 give the same 1626545 steps, fast 146 ms and 91 ms. So with the same orbit, the same size of numbers and the same machine, only the seeds in 2^30 Z^8 collapse into one bucket. They do about 930 times the chain steps and are about 100 to 140 times slower. The slow case comes from the hash, not from the machine. Cleanup: node_modules, site/node_modules, packages/engine/node_modules and site/dist were deleted. Final git status --porcelain: 'A  packages/engine/test/unit/redteam-RT-03-hash.test.ts'. HEAD is still b9b8504. No server was started. incidental: the same linear hash gives only 2306 distinct values on 40000 positions even from (1,...,1), with a largest bucket of 120. This is a milder form of the same cause and does not change the verdict.
verdicts.reason: reproduced as stated; observed matches in substance (cap 40000: fast path 12.7 to 24.5 s against 0.52 to 1.18 s for the generic loop, 20.7 to 24.7 times, in three runs at load 3 to 20; cap 100000: 149.5 s against 2.9 s; the same items), and a bucket and chain-step count shows every position in 2^30 Z^8 hashing to one bucket (40000 in one bucket, 9194 comparisons per lookup against 9.9 for the seed (2^30+1)(1,...,1) of the same size); the claimed level of minor stands because the cap still ends the search with correct results, so the rubric names no item for a slowdown on an input no tool reaches
